scope: Finite-lower RANGE and ROWS MIN/MAX with bounded or unbounded-following upper endpoints
contracts: Scalar integer, Bool and date/time comparisons match aggregate selectors; Decimal AggrMin/AggrMax and CompareValues both compare signed Int128, including NaN/Inf encodings.
Admitted optional values have one optional layer over unboxed scalars, so missing values are excluded and populated optional outputs reuse the scalar representation.
Collector queue contains a contiguous fetched tail; Fetched minus Buffer.Size gives its absolute origin after each public collector cleanup.
Absolute RANGE bounds advance monotonically; expiring before inserting and retaining maximum SeenEnd handles peer batches, sparse empty gaps and clipped tails without re-entry.
Input Yield does not advance candidates; collector retains partially fetched rows, and Fetched increments only for successful input rows.
Collector factory owns comparator state for the wrapper lifetime; each stream retains its own queue, bounds, candidates and context.
Candidate elements use MiniKQL allocation; circular-buffer growth charges transient old-plus-new storage and rolls back new charges if reserve throws; OffloadAlloc checks limits before charging.
Completion clears candidates and queue and resets accounted bytes; early stream destruction clears its queue and frees outstanding accounting.

Compiler maps names to indices after type annotation; runtime checks unique output indices, scalar type equality, exactly one RANGE interval, a finite lower endpoint and any infinite upper endpoint directed Following.
Existing collector deserializer and comparator conversion are reused, preserving sort direction, nullable keys and supported key-type boundary semantics.
MIN/MAX-only windows bypass the outer collector and frame fold; mixed aggregates/native functions retain their existing final path and read overwritten MIN/MAX output fields.
All added/changed production paths are in ydb/core/kqp; yql/essentials is read-only evidence.

For unbounded following, the existing collector performs the required initial input drain. RANGE then expires deque entries as the finite lower bound advances; ROWS initializes its two-stack state once and performs expiry/transfer without new entering rows.
Existing running, whole-partition and current-row ROWS suffix special dispatch remains unchanged; eligibility widening only reaches the general ROWS path for other finite lower suffixes.

The mutable computation node depends on its input FromFlow node, matching the existing WinFramesCollector dependency path. Each invalidated partition obtains a fresh stream value with independent bounds, ordinals and candidate state.
limits: No C++ compilation, SQL parser execution, native collector invocation or runtime execution was performed.
Native tests must still exercise yield, cancellation, per-partition recreation, resource accounting and memory-limit failures.
Public buffer Reserve uses vector resizing; actual allocator overhead and measured peak memory still require native evidence.
Excluded scalar/value families keep their original algorithms; full Q01 remains subject to scope assessment and native acceptance.
SQL generator has typed scalar, null, peer, descending, sparse and mixed controls; Decimal special encodings are source-reviewed only.
Mixed aggregates/native functions use two collectors; peer-dense and suffix partitions can approach two buffered row arrays plus candidates, and require peak-memory and lookahead measurement.
